description: NasaResearch is searching for different places in which bases in the moon can be constructed.
summary:
This project developed a comparative assessment of five terrestrial analog sites that could help scientists prepare for future Moon and Mars missions. The selected locations are the McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica, Lanzarote and Río Tinto in Spain, the Namib Desert in Namibia, and the Lofoten Islands in Norway. Each site was evaluated using the Terrestrial Analog Suitability Index (TASI), a project-created model based on topography, geology, environmental conditions, and available resources.
The project addresses the challenge by identifying and comparing Earth environments that share specific characteristics with the Moon or Mars. A global map presents their location and scientific relevance. This research is important because terrestrial analogs allow scientists to study planetary processes, test exploration technologies, and improve mission preparation before sending equipment and astronauts beyond Earth.
details:
This project identifies and compares five locations on Earth with characteristics similar to the Moon or Mars. It uses the Terrestrial Analog Suitability Index (TASI), a scoring model created for this project that evaluates each site based on four factors: topography, geology, environmental conditions, and available resources. The results are presented in a global map showing each location and its scientific relevance.

The main benefit is helping scientists identify places to study planetary environments and test exploration technologies before future space missions. Its intended impact is to support research and improve preparation for lunar and Martian exploration.

The project uses public scientific data from NASA, ESA, and research publications, along with digital mapping and image-generation tools. Its creative aspect is combining scientific research, a custom evaluation model, and a global map. The main factors considered were geological similarity, terrain, extreme conditions, and resources such as minerals and subsurface ice. Earth cannot fully reproduce the conditions of the Moon or Mars, but these sites provide useful comparisons.
